1. (Currently amended) A method, comprising: transmitting a sequence of light pulses having a first speed; receiving a second sequence of light pulses from a vehicle; and transmitting a message as a sequence of light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the method is performed by a non-transitory computer-readable medium storing executable instructions.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first speed, and wherein the computing device is implemented on a processor executing instructions stored in non-transitory memory.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity based on a threshold number of consecutive failed light pulse receptions, and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of light pulses from a third vehicle and determines a fourth speed based on comparing the second sequence and the third sequence, and transmits the message as a sequence of light pulses having the fourth speed, wherein the fourth speed is different from the second speed and is selected based on a priority weighting of the received sequences.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

6. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed.

7. (Original) The method of claim 6, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

8. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor.

9. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from two or more vehicles.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 9, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth speed based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth speed is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses, and wherein the emitting step is performed by a processor executing non-transitory stored instructions.

11. (Currently amended) An apparatus, comprising: a processor; a non-transitory memory, the non-transitory memory storing instructions executable by the processor to: transmit a sequence of light pulses having a first speed; receive a second sequence of light pulses from a vehicle; and transmit a message as a sequence of light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed.

12. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first speed, and wherein the computing device comprises the processor executing instructions from the non-transitory memory.

13. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 12, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity based on a threshold number of consecutive failed light pulse receptions, and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed.

14. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 13, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of light pulses from a third vehicle and determines a fourth speed based on comparing the second sequence and the third sequence, and transmits the message as a sequence of light pulses having the fourth speed, wherein the fourth speed is different from the second speed and is selected based on a priority weighting of the received sequences.

15. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

16. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed.

17. (Original) The apparatus of claim 16, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

18. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor.

19. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from one or more vehicles.

20. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 19, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth speed based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth speed is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses, and wherein the emitting is performed by the processor executing instructions from the non-transitory memory.
